title: Faith, hope, love at work (1 Thessalonians 1)
hook: Paul remembers their work of faith, labor of love, patience of hope
tomorrow: give thanks in everything? even on the worst day of the week?

segments.voice: Yesterday, put on love: a wardrobe of compassion, kindness and patience, with love on top, worn by people already called beloved. Yesterday's line: above all, love.

Old work gloves tell on their owner. A hole worn through at the thumb, a stiff patch from a paint can, a palm gone smooth from years on the same handle. So do a coach's whistle, a nurse's shoes, a baker's burned knuckles. Nobody needs a speech about what those hands did. A letter to the church in Thessalonica opens the same way. Paul, with Silvanus and Timothy, doesn't start by correcting anyone. He gives thanks, and starts with what he remembers seeing them do.
screen: `GLOVES TELL ON THEIR OWNER.` → `NO SPEECH NEEDED.` → `WHAT PAUL REMEMBERS.`

segments.voice: Here's the line: "Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ." Three pairs, and each ties a big word to something you could see. Faith shows up as work. Love shows up as labor, the effort that leaves a person tired. Hope shows up as patience, staying put under pressure. Faith, hope and love: the same three Paul names together in First Corinthians thirteen. Here they've got their sleeves rolled up. And it costs something. They "received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost." Trouble and joy in one sentence. And look at the direction it took. Paul says they "turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God." Turned, and then served: faith with somewhere to go and something to do. Then a sound picture: "For from you sounded out the word of the Lord." Other towns were already telling Paul about them, so much that he says he doesn't need to say a thing. In this letter faith isn't only a private opinion. It's a reputation other people can describe, the way a pair of gloves can.
screen: `WORK OF FAITH.` · `LABOR OF LOVE.` · `PATIENCE OF HOPE.` · `IT SOUNDED OUT.` · then, large: `WORK, LABOR, PATIENCE.`

segments.voice: Turn your hands palm up in your lap and look at them: the lines, a scar, a callus, whatever is there. Let one person come to mind whose hands you've watched do faithful work, and name one thing they did that was work, one that was labor, and one that was patience. No need to say anything aloud; give each one a slow breath, and keep your hands open the whole time.
Faith. In First Thessalonians one, not only something held inside, but something you can see: a work of faith, beside love's labor and hope's patience, loud enough that other towns heard about it.
Your line: work, labor, patience. Faith, love and hope, each with its sleeves rolled up. That's today.

chat.says: found pop's work gloves packing his garage. holes in the fingers. he fixed half the church's porches. is that faith?
options: Paul would call it a work of faith: trust you can see in what someone's hands do.
Not really. Faith is what he believes inside; fixing porches is just being handy.
That's love, not faith. Paul keeps faith in the head and love in the hands.
chat.meaning: Paul remembers their work of faith, labor of love, patience of hope: each big word tied to something people could see them do.

Thessalonica.meaning: a city in Macedonia whose church received Paul's letters

Silvanus.meaning: a coworker of Paul named at the letter's opening

Holy Ghost.meaning: the King James name for the Holy Spirit

notes: Senses shape: the gloves in the hook and the hands in the practice carry the idea (faith you can see). The gloves are the writer's picture, not from the text.
'Labor, the effort that leaves a person tired' and 'patience, staying put under pressure' are plain glosses of κόπος and ὑπομονή; confirm.
'He doesn't need to say a thing' paraphrases 1:8 ('so that we need not to speak any thing').
1 Corinthians 13:13 ('faith, hope, charity, these three') cited for 'the same three Paul names together'; confirm the link is fairly put.
Thessalonica glossed as in Macedonia (the chapter names Macedonia and Achaia, 1:7); confirm.
